inputs.name: ticks

inputs.name: action

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

device.name: nav-suite depth navigation (Anymal D, Isaac Lab)

facts.text: The suite registers three Gymnasium task ids whose entry point is isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv
The DEV task id NavTasks-DepthImgNavigation-PPO-Anymal-D-DEV uses NavTasksDepthNavEnvCfg_DEV
The scene robot is ANYMAL_D_CFG at the prim path {ENV_REGEX_NS}/Robot
The high-level action term velocity_command is a NavigationSE2ActionCfg
NavigationSE2ActionCfg has action_dim 3 (vx, vy, omega) and clip_mode none, so the action is not clipped
The high-level planner runs at 10 Hz and decimation is int(200 / 10) = 20, so one environment step advances 0.1 s
The reset event randomizes the base yaw over (-3.0, 3.0)
The reset event sets the joint position and velocity ranges to (0.0, 0.0)
The timeout termination uses max_speed 1.0 and safety_factor 4.0
The goal_reached termination requires 2.0 s within distance 0.5, angle 0.3 and speed 0.6
Contact of the base or of a thigh, hip or shank with the environment terminates the episode
The policy observation group concatenates base linear and angular velocity, joint positions and velocities, goal commands and an embedded depth image, with corruption disabled

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial yaw and the integration is deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream reset uses the Isaac Lab/torch random generators and this package's fake uses Python's random.Random, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: Isaac Sim 4.5, Isaac Lab 2.1, a GPU and the git-lfs policy and terrain assets are not available where the gate runs; the fake backend is a pure-Python kinematic SE2 model with no dynamics (no rigid-body motion, contacts, friction, actuator or sensor model), not the physics simulation, and it was never compared with an upstream run

the observation is the planar pose [x, y, yaw] only; the upstream policy group concatenates base velocities, joint positions and velocities, goal commands and an embedded depth image, so the image and the joint state are not covered
the registered task is vectorized (the DEV config sets num_envs 2); the fake serves one unbatched environment, and its reward is 0 every step because the upstream reward terms are not modelled
the fake truncates at 200 steps (episode_length_s 20 s divided by the 0.1 s step) and does not model the proportional timeout, the goal_reached or the base/leg contact terminations
the reset yaw draw uses Python's random.Random and the upstream event uses the Isaac Lab/torch random generators, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
